title: Interface Segregation
summary: Many small interfaces beat one fat one: no class should implement methods it cannot use.

steps.title: The fat interface
body: public void Scan(string doc) => throw new NotSupportedException();
public void Fax(string doc)  => throw new NotSupportedException();

`BasicPrinter` is forced to "implement" things it cannot do, which is an LSP landmine. And every client that only prints still depends on `Scan` and `Fax`: change the fax signature and all of them recompile.
The **Interface Segregation Principle**: clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use.

options: It must implement `Scan` and `Fax` even though it cannot, so callers can be surprised by exceptions

steps.title: Role interfaces
body: class BasicPrinter : IPrinter { public void Print(string doc) => Console.WriteLine(doc); }
class OfficeMachine : IPrinter, IScanner, IFax { /* all three */ }

A method that prints asks for an `IPrinter`, and works with both machines. A class implements exactly the roles it can fill. The .NET library does this too: `IEnumerable<T>`, `ICollection<T>`, `IList<T>` and `IReadOnlyList<T>` are separate so a method can ask for only what it needs.

steps.prompt: A method only loops over items. Which parameter type follows ISP best?
steps.explain: It asks for the smallest role that does the job, so callers can pass a list, an array, a set or a LINQ query.

steps.prompt: Which role interface does each method belong in?
Make the robot implement only the roles it can fill.
code: class Human : IWorker__1__ IEater { public void Work() { } public void Eat() { } }
void Use(IPrinter p) { p.Print("A"); if (p is IScanner s) s.Scan("B"); }
public void Print(string d) => Console.Write("print " + d + " ");
public void Scan(string d) => Console.Write("scan " + d);

steps.title: Split the fat interface
prompt: - `interface IPrinter { string Print(string doc); }` and `interface IScanner { string Scan(string doc); }`
starter: public string Scan(string doc) => throw new NotSupportedException();
template: IPrinter[] dojoPrinters = { new BasicPrinter(), new OfficeMachine() };
Dojo.Eq("both print", new List<string> { "printed a", "printed a" }, dojoPrinters.Select(p => p.Print("a")).ToList());
Dojo.Check("BasicPrinter is not a scanner", !typeof(IScanner).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(BasicPrinter)), "BasicPrinter still claims to scan");
